To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the levels of immunoreactive dynorphin-(1-13)- and dynorphin-( 1-8) peptides are decreased in the suprachaismatic nucleus of spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) and that the level of ir-dynorphin-(1 13) is increased in the substantia Nigra of SHR compared with Wistar-Kyoto rats (WKY).

(1) the levels of dynorphin-like immunoreactivity (ir) in the suprachiastic nucleus, paraventricular nucleus and central amygdale of spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) were decreased; (2) the level of ir-dynorphin-(1-13)-like immunoreactivity (1-13) was decreased in the neurointermediary lobe of SHR; (3) the level of 1-13-ir was decreased in
dynorphin 2-8 and leu-enkphalin are present in brain and pituitary in SHR and WKY, and that the distribution of dynorphins and leucine enkephalin is different in SHR compared to WKY.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of dynorphins and leucine-enkephalin, in the central nervous system and pituitary, of normotensive and spontaneously hypertensive rat strains.
the possible involvement of opioid peptides in the regulation of blood pressure in SHR rats.
the possible role of opioid peptides in the central control of blood pressure in the spontaneously hypertensive rat (SHR) and its normotensive control, the Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the distribution of ir-dynorphins is different from that of ir-Leu-enkephalins in the various brain nuclei and that there is a differential distribution in the various brain areas of the two strains of rats studied.
SHR rats have a decreased level of Dyn-1-13 and Dyn-1-8 in some brain areas, but an increased level in others.
the differences observed between SHR and WKy rats in the distribution of these opioid peptides in the brain are not consistent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the levels of ir-DYN and LE in the brain and pituitary differ between SHR and normotensive rats.
the dynorphins and LE in the NIL of SHR rats were decreased compared to WKY rats.

the dynorphin peptides are more widely distributed and have a more complex pattern than the Leu-enkephalins, and the dynorphin-like immunoreactivity is more abundant than Leu-enkepahalin-like immunoreactivity in the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynorphin 13-16 and dynorphin 7-8 are not the only active forms of dynorphin in the brain.
the distribution and concentration of ir-DYN, ir-DYN-(1-8, ir-LE in the brain and pituitary are altered in SHR rats.
there are differences in the levels of dynorphins in the brain between WKY and SHR, and that these levels may be important in understanding the pathogenesis of hypertension.
